In [[differential geometry]] a '''Rizza manifold''', named after [[Giovanni Battista Rizza]],<ref name="Ich88">The dedication of the work {{harv|Ichijyō|1988|p=1}} reads:-"''Dedicated to professor G. B. Rizza, who is the originator of the notion of Rizza manifolds.''"</ref> is an [[almost complex manifold]] also supporting a [[Finsler manifold|Finsler structure]]: this kind of manifold is also referred as '''almost Hermitian Finsler manifold'''.<ref>See {{harv|Ichijyō|1988|p=6}}.</ref>

==History==

The history of Rizza manifolds follows the history of the structure that such objects carry. According to {{harvs|txt|last=Kobayashi|first=Shoshichi|authorlink=Shoshichi Kobayashi | year=1975|p=153}}, the geometry of [[Linear complex structure|complex]] [[Finsler manifold|Finsler structures]] was first studied in Rizza's 1964 paper "F-forme quadratiche ed hermitiane", but Rizza announced his results nearly two years before, in the short communications {{harv|Rizza|1962a}} and {{harv|Rizza|1962b}}, proving them in the article {{harv|Rizza|1963}}, nearly one year earlier than the one cited by Kobayashi. Rizza called this differential geometric structure, defined on [[Dimension (mathematics)|even-dimensional]] [[manifold]]s, "Struttura di Finsler quasi Hermitiana":<ref>"''Almost Hermitian Finsler structure''": see  {{harv|Rizza|1962b|pp=271, 273–274}} and {{harv|Rizza|1963|pp=83, 90–91}}.</ref> his motivation for the introduction of the concept seems to be the aim of comparing two different structures existing on the same manifold.<ref>{{harvtxt|Rizza|1962b|p=1}} himself states:-"L'esistenza di strutture di tipo diverso su una medesima varietà dà sempre luogo a problemi di confronto (The existence of structures of different kind on the same manifold always gives rise to comparison problems)".</ref> Later {{Harvtxt|Ichijyō|1988|p=1}} started calling this structure "''Rizza structure''", and manifolds carrying it "''Rizza manifolds''".<ref name="Ich88"/>

==Formal definition==
The content of this paragraph closely follows references {{harv|Rizza|1963}} and {{Harv|Ichijyō|1988}}, borrowing the scheme of notation equally from both sources. Precisely, given a [[differentiable manifold]] <math>M</math> and one of its [[Point (geometry)|points]] <math>x\in M</math>,
*<math>TM</math> is the [[tangent bundle]] of <math>M</math>;
*<math>T_xM</math> is the [[tangent space]] at <math>x</math>;

{{EquationRef|1|Definition 1.}} Let <math>M</math> be a <math>2n</math>-[[Dimension (mathematics)|dimensional]] [[Finsler manifold]], <math>n\ge 1</math>, and let <math>F:TM\to\R</math> its Finsler function. If the condition

:{{EquationRef|2|(1){{spaces|5}}}}<math>F(x,cy)=|c|F(x,y)\qquad\forall c\in\mathbb{C},\quad x\in M,\quad y\in T_xM</math>

holds true, then <math>M</math> is a '''Rizza manifold'''.
